newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCI says jobs data points to need for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: ACCI says jobs data points to need for rate cut.

text.p: The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry said on Thursday weak job figures issued earlier showed interest rates might have to fall.
"There is also a clear message in these figures for the Reserve Bank," the Chamber's chief executive Mark Paterson said in a statement.
"The aim of policy should be faster economic growth which will bring with it faster employment growth," Paterson said.
"Official interest rates, if they move at all, should move downwards and not up," he said.

Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate fell marginally to 8.7 percent from 8.8 percent in February, compared with 8.5 percent for the same month a year earlier, the statistics bureau said on Thursday.
Employment fell 33,900 in March to 8.38 million, compared with expectations for a rise of around 13,500.

GDP grew 0.5 percent in the December quarter for annual growth of 3.1 percent and must accelerate markedly to meet the government's forecast of 3.5 percent year-average growth in the fiscal year to June.
Treasurer Peter Costello has said there are signs, such as an upturn in the housing sector, that point to improving prospects for stronger economic growth in 1997.
The Reserve Bank cut its overnight cash rate three times between July and December last year, each time cutting it by 50 basis points to stand at 6.0 percent.
